chunks.en: You've probably heard that AI just predicts the next word.
chunks.zh: 你可能听说过：AI 只是在预测下一个词。

chunks.en: That's true.
chunks.zh: 这没错。

chunks.en: But it's also where most explanations stop.
chunks.zh: 但大多数解释也就讲到这里为止。

chunks.en: In September 2024, OpenAI tested two of its models on the AIME,
chunks.zh: 2024 年 9 月，OpenAI 拿自己的两个模型去考 AIME，

chunks.en: a hard American math competition.
chunks.zh: 一场很难的美国数学竞赛。

chunks.en: The older model, GPT-4o, solved about 12 percent of the problems.
chunks.zh: 老模型 GPT-4o，只做对了大约 12% 的题。

chunks.en: The newer one, called o1, solved 74 percent.
chunks.zh: 新模型 o1，做对了 74%。

chunks.en: Both of them still work by predicting the next word.
chunks.zh: 两个模型靠的都还是预测下一个词。

chunks.en: The difference is that one of them learned to think before it answers.
chunks.zh: 区别在于，其中一个学会了先想再答。

chunks.en: Let's start with what the model actually sees.
chunks.zh: 先看模型真正看到的是什么。

chunks.en: Not letters. Not words. Numbers.
chunks.zh: 不是字母，不是单词，是数字。

chunks.en: Your text gets chopped into pieces called tokens.
chunks.zh: 你输入的文字，会被切成一块一块，叫作 token。

chunks.en: In English, a token is about four characters,
chunks.zh: 在英文里，一个 token 大约是 4 个字符，

chunks.en: or roughly three quarters of a word.
chunks.zh: 差不多是四分之三个单词。

chunks.en: Each token is then swapped for an ID number.
chunks.zh: 然后，每个 token 都会被换成一个编号。

chunks.en: From here on, the model never sees your words again.
chunks.zh: 从这一步开始，模型再也看不到你的字了，

chunks.en: Only these numbers.
chunks.zh: 只看得到这些数字。

chunks.en: That's why AI can stumble on things that feel trivial to us,
chunks.zh: 所以 AI 可能会在一些我们觉得很简单的事上出错，

chunks.en: like counting the letters in a word.
chunks.zh: 比如数一个单词里有几个字母。

chunks.en: It never saw the letters.
chunks.zh: 因为它根本没看到过那些字母。

chunks.en: So what does the model do with those numbers?
chunks.zh: 那模型拿这些数字做什么？

chunks.en: Just one job, over and over:
chunks.zh: 只做一件事，一遍又一遍：

chunks.en: given everything so far, what comes next?
chunks.zh: 根据前面所有内容，下一个是什么？

chunks.en: For every possible next token, it gives a probability.
chunks.zh: 对每一个可能出现的下一个 token，它都会给出一个概率。

chunks.en: After "The cat sat on the," the word "mat" might score high,
chunks.zh: 在 "The cat sat on the" 后面，"mat" 的概率可能很高，

chunks.en: "floor" a bit lower, and "banana" almost zero.
chunks.zh: "floor" 低一点，"banana" 几乎为零。

chunks.en: It picks one, adds it to the end, and asks the same question again.
chunks.zh: 它选一个，接到末尾，然后再问同一个问题。

chunks.en: Token by token,
chunks.zh: 一个 token 接一个 token，

chunks.en: that's how every answer you've ever gotten from a chatbot was built.
chunks.zh: 你从聊天机器人那里得到的每一个回答，都是这样拼出来的。

chunks.en: A long answer can take hundreds or even thousands of these predictions,
chunks.zh: 一个长回答，可能要做几百甚至几千次这样的预测，

chunks.en: each one depending on everything that came before it.
chunks.zh: 每一次都取决于前面所有的内容。

chunks.en: And it doesn't always pick the top choice.
chunks.zh: 而且它不一定选概率最高的那个。

chunks.en: A little randomness is usually built in,
chunks.zh: 通常会加一点随机性，

chunks.en: which is why the same question can get two different answers.
chunks.zh: 所以同一个问题问两次，答案可能不一样。

chunks.en: So far, this is the explanation you've heard before.
chunks.zh: 到这里，都是你以前听过的解释。

chunks.en: The interesting part is where those probabilities come from.
chunks.zh: 真正有意思的，是这些概率从哪里来。

chunks.en: Inside the model are billions of numbers called parameters.
chunks.zh: 模型里面有几十亿个数字，叫作参数。

chunks.en: GPT-3, back in 2020, had 175 billion of them.
chunks.zh: 2020 年的 GPT-3，就有 1750 亿个。

chunks.en: So how does it decide which earlier words matter?
chunks.zh: 那它怎么判断前面哪些词重要？

chunks.en: Inside, each token becomes a long list of numbers,
chunks.zh: 在模型内部，每个 token 都会变成一长串数字，

chunks.en: and those lists pass through layer after layer.
chunks.zh: 这些数字一层一层地往上传。

chunks.en: In each layer, every token can look back at the tokens before it,
chunks.zh: 在每一层里，每个 token 都可以回头看前面的 token，

chunks.en: and pull in the ones that are relevant.
chunks.zh: 把相关的那些信息拉过来。

chunks.en: Take this sentence: "The cat sat on the mat because it was tired."
chunks.zh: 比如这句话："The cat sat on the mat because it was tired."（猫坐在垫子上，因为它累了。）

chunks.en: To make sense of "it," the model has to connect it back to "cat," not "mat."
chunks.zh: 要理解 "it"，模型得把它连回 "cat"，而不是 "mat"。

chunks.en: This step is called attention.
chunks.zh: 这一步叫作“注意力”。

chunks.en: It comes from a 2017 paper by researchers at Google,
chunks.zh: 它来自 2017 年谷歌研究者的一篇论文，

chunks.en: titled "Attention Is All You Need,"
chunks.zh: 题目就叫《Attention Is All You Need》，

chunks.en: and it's the core of the design behind today's large language models.
chunks.zh: 是今天大语言模型设计的核心。

chunks.en: At the start, all those parameters are random,
chunks.zh: 一开始，所有这些参数都是随机的，

chunks.en: and the model's guesses are nonsense.
chunks.zh: 模型猜出来的全是胡话。

chunks.en: Training is a guessing game.
chunks.zh: 训练就是一场猜词游戏：

chunks.en: Show the model real text, hide the next token, let it guess,
chunks.zh: 给模型看真实的文字，把下一个 token 遮住，让它猜，

chunks.en: then nudge every parameter slightly toward the right answer.
chunks.zh: 然后把每个参数都往正确答案的方向轻轻推一点。

chunks.en: Then do it again. And again.
chunks.zh: 然后再来一次，再来一次。

chunks.en: Meta's Llama 3 was trained on more than 15 trillion tokens.
chunks.zh: Meta 的 Llama 3，训练用了超过 15 万亿个 token。

chunks.en: To put that in perspective:
chunks.zh: 换个说法：

chunks.en: a person reading nonstop, at an average reading speed,
chunks.zh: 一个人以正常速度不停地读，

chunks.en: would need roughly 90,000 years to get through that much text.
chunks.zh: 大约要读 9 万年才能读完这么多文字。

chunks.en: And here's the surprising part.
chunks.zh: 意外的地方在这里：

chunks.en: To get good at guessing the next word across all that text,
chunks.zh: 为了在这么多文字上都猜得准，

chunks.en: the model ends up picking up grammar, facts,
chunks.zh: 模型顺带学会了语法、事实，

chunks.en: and patterns of reasoning along the way.
chunks.zh: 还有推理的套路。

chunks.en: Nobody programmed those in.
chunks.zh: 没有人把这些写进程序。

chunks.en: They're a side effect of getting good at guessing.
chunks.zh: 它们是“猜得准”的副产品。

chunks.en: But a model trained only this way has a strange problem.
chunks.zh: 但只这样训练出来的模型，有个奇怪的毛病。

chunks.en: It's an autocomplete for the internet.
chunks.zh: 它是一台“互联网自动补全机”。

chunks.en: Ask it a question, and it might just write more questions,
chunks.zh: 你问它一个问题，它可能接着写出更多问题，

chunks.en: the way a quiz or a homework sheet would carry on.
chunks.zh: 就像一张测验卷或作业纸会一直往下列题。

chunks.en: Turning it into an assistant takes a second, much smaller round of training.
chunks.zh: 要把它变成助手，还需要第二轮训练，规模小得多。

chunks.en: People write example answers and rank the model's replies,
chunks.zh: 人先写出示范回答，再给模型的回答排名次，

chunks.en: and the model is tuned toward the ones people prefer.
chunks.zh: 然后把模型往人更喜欢的方向调。

chunks.en: Ranking is the clever part.
chunks.zh: 排名次是最巧的地方：

chunks.en: It's much easier for a person to say which of two answers is better
chunks.zh: 让人说出两个回答哪个更好，

chunks.en: than to write the perfect answer themselves.
chunks.zh: 比让人自己写出完美的回答容易得多。

chunks.en: In 2022, OpenAI showed how powerful this step is.
chunks.zh: 2022 年，OpenAI 证明了这一步有多厉害：

chunks.en: People preferred answers from a 1.3 billion parameter model trained this way
chunks.zh: 经过这种训练的 13 亿参数模型，

chunks.en: over the 175 billion parameter GPT-3.
chunks.zh: 回答比 1750 亿参数的 GPT-3 更受人喜欢。

chunks.en: A model more than 100 times smaller, and people liked it better.
chunks.zh: 小了一百多倍，人们却更喜欢它。

chunks.en: By 2023, that was the full story:
chunks.zh: 到了 2023 年，故事就是这样：

chunks.en: predict the next word, then get polished by human feedback.
chunks.zh: 先学会预测下一个词，再靠人的反馈打磨。

chunks.en: Then the story changed.
chunks.zh: 然后，故事变了。

chunks.en: Remember those math scores?
chunks.zh: 还记得那两个数学成绩吗？

chunks.en: 12 percent versus 74.
The key new ingredient was a different kind of training,
chunks.zh: 关键的新东西是另一种训练，

chunks.en: called reinforcement learning.
chunks.zh: 叫强化学习。

chunks.en: OpenAI hasn't published the details,
chunks.zh: OpenAI 没公开细节，

chunks.en: but here's the basic idea, as other labs have since described it.
chunks.zh: 但其他实验室后来公开过基本做法，是这样的：

chunks.en: Give the model a math problem.
chunks.zh: 给模型一道数学题，

chunks.en: Let it write out as much working as it wants before its final answer.
chunks.zh: 让它在给出最终答案之前，想写多少推演就写多少。

chunks.en: If the answer is right, reward it.
chunks.zh: 答对了就奖励，

chunks.en: If it's wrong, don't.
chunks.zh: 答错了就不奖励。

chunks.en: Nobody shows it how to reason.
chunks.zh: 没有人教它怎么推理，

chunks.en: It only finds out whether it got the answer right.
chunks.zh: 它只知道自己最后答没答对。

chunks.en: In January 2025, the Chinese lab DeepSeek published
chunks.zh: 2025 年 1 月，中国公司 DeepSeek 公开了

chunks.en: what happened when they trained a model this way.
chunks.zh: 他们用这种方法训练模型的结果。

chunks.en: On that same math competition,
chunks.zh: 在同一场数学竞赛上，

chunks.en: the model's score climbed from 15.6 percent to 71 percent
chunks.zh: 模型的分数从 15.6% 涨到了 71%，

chunks.en: over the course of training.
chunks.zh: 在训练过程中。

chunks.en: And it started doing things nobody had taught it.
chunks.zh: 而且它开始做一些没人教过它的事：

chunks.en: It spent longer thinking on each problem.
chunks.zh: 每道题想得越来越久，

chunks.en: It went back and checked its own steps.
chunks.zh: 还会回头检查自己的步骤。

chunks.en: At one point, in the middle of a solution, it wrote:
chunks.zh: 有一次解题解到一半，它写下：

chunks.en: "Wait, wait. Wait."
chunks.zh: "Wait, wait. Wait."（等等，等等。等一下。）

chunks.en: Then it found its own mistake.
chunks.zh: 然后它找到了自己的错误。

chunks.en: The researchers called it an "aha moment."
chunks.zh: 研究者把这叫作“顿悟时刻”。

chunks.en: By the spring of 2025, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic and Google
chunks.zh: 到 2025 年春天，OpenAI、DeepSeek、Anthropic 和谷歌

chunks.en: had all released models that can think before they answer.
chunks.zh: 都已经推出了会先想再答的模型。

chunks.en: And OpenAI reported something else:
chunks.zh: OpenAI 还发现了一件事：

chunks.en: the longer the model is allowed to think, the better it tends to do.
chunks.zh: 允许模型想得越久，它往往做得越好。

chunks.en: That's what is happening when a chatbot pauses
chunks.zh: 当聊天机器人停下来、

chunks.en: and shows you a "thinking" label.
chunks.zh: 显示“正在思考”的时候，发生的就是这件事：

chunks.en: It's writing out its working before it shows you the answer.
chunks.zh: 它在给你答案之前，先把推演写出来。

chunks.en: And that working isn't free.
chunks.zh: 而这些推演不是免费的。

chunks.en: Every thinking token has to be predicted, just like the answer.
chunks.zh: 每一个“思考”的 token 都要像答案一样被预测出来。

chunks.en: On OpenAI's API, those reasoning tokens are billed as output,
chunks.zh: 在 OpenAI 的 API 上，这些推理 token 和答案一样按输出计费，

chunks.en: even though you never see them.
chunks.zh: 哪怕你根本看不到它们。

chunks.en: That's why thinking mode is slower,
chunks.zh: 所以思考模式更慢，

chunks.en: and why it often costs more.
chunks.zh: 也常常更贵。

chunks.en: So here's the part most explanations miss.
chunks.zh: 所以，大多数解释漏掉的是这一点。

chunks.en: AI still just predicts the next word.
chunks.zh: AI 还是只在预测下一个词。

chunks.en: That never changed.
chunks.zh: 这一点从来没变。

chunks.en: What changed is what it's predicting.
chunks.zh: 变的是它在预测什么：

chunks.en: Not just what someone on the internet would write next,
chunks.zh: 不只是网上的人下一句会写什么，

chunks.en: but the steps that lead to a right answer.
chunks.zh: 而是通往正确答案的那些步骤。

chunks.en: The thinking is made of the same tokens, one at a time.
chunks.zh: 那些“思考”，也是由同样的 token 一个一个组成的。

chunks.en: It's next-word prediction, pointed at a goal.
chunks.zh: 它还是在预测下一个词，只是有了目标。

chunks.en: So the whole recipe has three stages.
chunks.zh: 所以整套做法分三步：

chunks.en: First, guess the next word across trillions of tokens.
chunks.zh: 第一，在几万亿个 token 上猜下一个词；

chunks.en: Second, get polished by human preferences.
chunks.zh: 第二，按人的喜好打磨；

chunks.en: Third, get rewarded for reaching right answers.
chunks.zh: 第三，答对了就奖励。

chunks.en: Most explanations stop after the first two.
chunks.zh: 大多数解释讲完前两步就停了。

chunks.en: The third is the one that changed what AI can do.
chunks.zh: 真正改变 AI 能力的，是第三步。

chunks.en: What does this mean for you?
chunks.zh: 这和你有什么关系？

chunks.en: First, for hard problems, like math, code, or planning,
chunks.zh: 第一，遇到难题，比如数学、写代码、做计划，

chunks.en: use the thinking mode if your AI has one.
chunks.zh: 如果你的 AI 有思考模式，就打开它。

chunks.en: It's the same kind of machine, given time to think.
chunks.zh: 还是同一类机器，只是给了它思考的时间。

chunks.en: Second, thinking isn't the same as knowing.
chunks.zh: 第二，会思考不等于知道。

chunks.en: Its knowledge still comes from patterns in its training,
chunks.zh: 它的知识还是来自训练里学到的规律，

chunks.en: so it can reason carefully and still be wrong.
chunks.zh: 所以它可能推得很认真，结果还是错的。

chunks.en: Check anything that matters.
chunks.zh: 重要的事，自己核实一下。

chunks.en: So here's my question.
chunks.zh: 最后问你一个问题：

chunks.en: When an AI writes "wait, let me check that," is it really thinking?
chunks.zh: 当 AI 写下“等等，我检查一下”的时候，它是真的在思考，

chunks.en: Or is it just a very good prediction of what thinking looks like?
chunks.zh: 还是只是非常擅长预测“思考看起来是什么样子”？

chunks.en: Tell me in the comments.
chunks.zh: 评论区告诉我。
